en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew leaves the object unstated.

01.r: Samuel begins his warning to the people.

02.r: Points ahead to the list that follows.

03.r: What a king will in fact do.

04.r: How a king will behave: his settled practice toward his subjects.
04.n: The word usually means judgment or justice (Gesenius, BDB), but STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense custom, manner. The DRC's 'the right of the king' follows the other sense: what a king may claim.

05.r: The king the people have asked for.

07.r: He will be king over them.
07.n: Gesenius: to reign, to be king, followed by 'over', and cites the chapter's earlier 1 Sa. 8:7 for that construction.

08.r: Over the whole people Samuel is addressing.

09.r: Marks 'your sons' as the object of 'take'.
09.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'your sons'.

10.r: The sons of the families of Israel.
10.n: The phrase comes first in the Hebrew, before its verb, so the stress falls on what is taken: 'your sons he will take'. YLT keeps that order.

11.r: The king will take their sons for his service.
11.n: A very common verb, as wide as English 'take'. It is the verb that runs through Samuel's whole list of what the king will take.

12.r: He will place the sons where he wants them.
12.n: Gesenius gives the general sense to put, to set, to place; STEPBible tags this occurrence 'appoint'. A perfect with 'and', carrying on the future before it; YLT renders the form literally, 'hath appointed'.

13.r: The sons will serve the king, not their families.

14.r: Service with the royal war chariots.
14.n: Gesenius: a chariot, especially a war chariot, and he cites this very form from this verse. The Hebrew is singular, 'his chariot'; read as a collective, his chariotry, it fits the translations' plural, but that is an inference.

15.r: Service with the king's mounted troops.
15.n: Gesenius: a horseman, citing this verse; the brief's lexicon and BDB give horse, steed. The BSB follows that sense with 'horses'.
t: and will make them his horsemen

16.r: Some of the sons will run on foot ahead of the chariots.
16.n: A perfect with 'and', carrying on the future; YLT renders it literally, 'have run'. Gesenius' entry notes figurative uses as well as the plain sense; here it is literal. The DRC adds 'his running footmen'.

17.r: Running ahead of the chariots as an escort.
17.n: Literally 'to the face of', the usual Hebrew way of saying 'before'.

18.r: The king's own chariot or chariotry.
18.n: Singular in the Hebrew, as earlier in the verse; the Geneva keeps the singular, 'his charet'.

_extra.18: αὐτοὺς (them): the Greek supplies the object that the Hebrew leaves unstated.

04.n: δικαίωμα, an ordinance, a right: the Greek reads the word in its legal sense, close to the DRC's 'the right of the king'.

12.n: θήσεται is the future middle of τίθημι, to put, set; the brief gives no dictionary form. The middle voice may carry the Hebrew 'for himself', which has no separate Greek word; that is an inference.

14.n: ἅρμα, chariot, plural in the Greek.

16.n: προτρέχω, to run ahead: one Greek word covers both 'run' and 'before'.
